messages:
incident-bot: :bangbang: Pager: high error rate and crashloops in us-east-1 model-serving pool. Symptoms: repeated container OOMs, CUDA driver errors, and rapid autoscaler churn. Severity: P1. Incident link: https://console.redwood.example/incidents/1768887777

Alex (oncall): spotting a spike in cuda errors and 137 exits on runtime pods. Error rate ~12% for chat endpoints. Kicking off triage.

Hiro-SRE: `kubectl get events` shows a flurry of `NodeNotReady` and `EvictionThreshold` events coincident with a surge of scale_up -> scale_down. Autoscaler target erratic.

Lina-MLInfra: looking at model memory heatmap: median memory per request jumped due to larger batch sizes from recent router config change. Also a batcher spike at 512. Suggest reverting router batch config and lowering max_batch to 64.

Ops-Aisha: can we put a temporary taint on new nodes to prevent scheduling while we debug? We can also disable scale-up to stop new bad nodes from joining.

Alex (oncall): applying taint to recent nodes: `kubectl taint nodes -l provision=autogen no-schedule=true:NoSchedule`

DeployBot: taint command executed by Alex (oncall) at 2025-12-02T18:11:10Z.

Hiro-SRE: found a subset of nodes with driver 470.x while cluster standard is 535.x — likely from an automated image rollout this morning. New nodes are allocating then failing CUDA allocations.

Lina-MLInfra: rolling model variant fallback to an L2 quantized model to reduce GPU memory per request: `servicectl update model-variant --region=us-east-1 --variant=quantized-l2`

Support-Kevin: customers reporting timeouts. Which orgs impacted? I can pre-stage messages.

CS-Maria: impacted customers list pulled: orgs A, C, F, plus a few trial users. Preparing message: "We're experiencing degraded inference in us-east-1; temporary failover enabled to reduce errors; engineering investigating."

PM-Diego: what's the blast radius for dedicated pools? We need to know if any enterprise SLAs are at risk.

Hiro-SRE: dedicated pools unaffected, they run on isolated nodes. This is hosted shared pool instability.

Alex (oncall): disabling aggressive cluster-autoscaler downscaling for now: `kubectl patch deployment cluster-autoscaler -n kube-system -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"autoscaler.kubernetes.io/disable-scale-down":"true"}}}}}'` -> applied.

Lina-MLInfra: after switching variants, error rate down from 12% -> 3.8% in ~6 minutes. CPU fallback shows higher latency but more successful responses.

Hiro-SRE: collecting kubelet logs from one problematic host: ```
Dec 02 18:05:43 ip-10-1-12 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 79, pid=2222, name=runtime-worker
Dec 02 18:05:43 ip-10-1-12 runtime: cuda error: driver shutdown
Dec 02 18:05:44 kubelet: Evicting pod "model-serving-abc" due to node memory pressure
```

Ops-Aisha: reprovisioning pipeline shows recent image hash `ami-202512` rolled out to some AZs. Rolling that back to `ami-202508` in the affected AZ.

DeployBot: rollback job started for us-east-1a. ETA 18 minutes.

Alex (oncall): routing 40% of traffic to eu-fallback region to reduce pressure: `redwood route split --from=hosted-us-east-1 --to=hosted-eu-west-1 --percent=40`

Support-Kevin: posting interim status to affected customers. Message: "Mitigations in place: traffic rerouted and fallback model variant active. We expect improvement; next update in 15m."

CS-Maria: sent messages to orgs A/C/F + trials. Added incident link.

Hiro-SRE: noticed autoscaler re-created a node pool with older kubelet + driver. Disable autoscaler scale-up for the pool that spawns older images: `kubectl label nodepool fast-autoscale autoscale-disabled=true`

Lina-MLInfra: also reducing router batch window to 100ms and max_batch 64 to limit memory amplification: `routerctl set batch-window 100ms --max-batch 64 --region us-east-1`

Alex (oncall): applied router changes. Observed immediate drop in per-request memory.

PM-Diego: request we track post-incident actions: 1) image gating for driver version, 2) autoscaler cooldown tuning, 3) router batch safety limits, 4) region spillover playbook.

Hiro-SRE: confirming: error rate now at 1.2%, latency back to near baseline for most customers. One AZ still showing elevated OOMs; drains ongoing.

Ops-Aisha: drains finishing for the tainted nodes. Cleaning up and queuing reprovision job against pipeline to repave the bad instances.

Alex (oncall): creating incident doc stub and collecting logs: `incidentctl create --id 1768887777 --severity P1 --summary "us-east-1 autoscale+driver mismatch -> OOMs"`

Support-Kevin: Customer comms updated: included note that dedicated customers unaffected and that a full root cause analysis will follow.

DeployBot: rollback complete in us-east-1a at 2025-12-02T18:28:30Z.

Hiro-SRE: action items assigned in incident tracker. Will schedule full postmortem.

Alex (oncall): handing off to Hiro-SRE for monitoring and follow-up for next 6 hours. Handoff notes: mitigations applied, router/variant changes, nodes cordoned and reprovision queued, customer messages sent.

Hiro-SRE: taking lead. Will monitor for 2 hours then move to backlog for detailed RCA.

incident-bot: Incident 1768887777 status: Mitigated. Will send reminders for postmortem planning.
